Question Choices: Fill: Solve the system using substitution: $y = 3x$ and $x + y = 16$. Enter $x, y$
Hints: Replace one variable with its equivalent expression, then solve and substitute back.
Solution: System: y=3 × x; x+y=16. Isolate y: y=(3)x+(0). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(1)[(3)x+(0)]=16. Combine: (4)x=16, so x=4. Then y=(3)(4)+(0)=12. Check both equations: -3(4)+1(12)=0; 1(4)+1(12)=16. Requested answer: 4,12.

Hints: Add equations when opposite coefficients cancel the requested variable.
Solution: System: 3 × x+y=12; 3 × x-y=6. Multiply equation 1 by 1 and equation 2 by 1, then add to cancel y: (6)x=18, so x=3. Substitute back to obtain y=3. Check both equations: 3(3)+1(3)=12; 3(3)+-1(3)=6. Adding cancels +y and −y. Subtracting would instead eliminate x, so the question specifies eliminating y. Requested answer: Add-equations.

Hints: Replace one variable with its equivalent expression, then solve and substitute back.
Solution: System: x=4; 3 × x+y=18. Isolate y: y=(-3)x+(18). Substitute into the other equation: (1)x+(0)[(-3)x+(18)]=4. Combine: (1)x=4, so x=4. Then y=(-3)(4)+(18)=6. Check both equations: 3(4)+1(6)=18; 1(4)+0(6)=4. Requested answer: 6.
